Stop agentic workflows from opening `[aw]` issues and posting security findings publicly

- Turn off gh-aw failure-report issues and the public `[aw] No-Op Runs` comments in every agentic workflow.
- Label the PR `ci-review-failed` / `ui-security-review-failed` when CI Review or UI Security Review produce no review; clear it on the next good run.
- List failed scheduled agentic runs in the weekly maintainer digest.
- Add `shared/security-findings.md`: security problems in released code go to the private triage Slack channel, never to an issue or comment.

Stop agentic workflows opening `[aw]` issues and posting security findings in public

Our agentic workflows open a new `[aw] …` issue for every failed run (about 40 in September, all closed by hand, e.g. #8817), and they post every `noop` message to the public #5685. For the UI Security Review that message is its threat analysis: on 22 Sep it spelled out an attack path in #6492 there. Nothing stopped a sweep from filing a vulnerability in released code as a public issue either.

### What changes

- **No more `[aw]` issues or No-Op comments.** `main` already sets `report-failure-as-issue: false` (#9574). This PR adds `noop.report-as-issue: false` and `create-issue: false` for `missing-tool`, `missing-data` and `report-incomplete` to every agentic workflow. Three workflows had the short `missing-tool: false` form, which gh-aw ignores in workflows that define their own safe-output jobs, so they now use the explicit form too.
- **A PR label instead.** When CI Review or UI Security Review produces no review (the agent failed, its output was never posted, or it ended without output, which leaves the run green), the PR gets `ci-review-failed` or `ui-security-review-failed`. The next good run removes it.
- **Failure counts go in the existing weekly spend report.** `agent-spend-report` already posts every agentic workflow's runs to the private Slack channel each Monday; its table gains a `failed` column, which covers the scheduled sweeps that have no PR to label.
- **Security findings in released code go to Slack.** New `shared/security-findings.md`, imported by the seven bug-filing workflows and the UI Security Review, gives the agent a `report_security_finding` output that posts to the triage channel via `PYDANTIC_AI_TRIAGE_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`, and tells it never to describe such a finding in an issue, comment, review or noop. Problems a PR introduces are still ordinary review comments.

### For reviewers

- The new secret use needed `gh aw compile --approve` (gh-aw's safe-update check); please confirm granting the triage webhook to these eight workflows.
- The security rule is a prompt instruction; nothing mechanically blocks an agent from filing publicly.
- Run artifacts and logs on this public repo still contain the agent transcript; that is out of scope here.

### Verification

- Locks recompiled with gh-aw v0.86.2 on current `main`: no action pin changes; every lock now has the failure, missing-tool and incomplete issue switches set to `false`; each lock's manifest differs from `main` only by the webhook secret in those eight workflows.
- `agentic_workflow_guard.py check --base-ref origin/main` passes; spend-report and guard tests pass (129), with a new test for the `failed` column; ruff and pyright clean.
- The label job and the Slack job have not run live yet; their first real run will be after merge.

### Checklist

- [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md).
- [x] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration, release note, and exact API-check waiver.
- [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases).

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Provision the failure labels before applying them**

On the first failed review in a repository where these new labels have not been created, this request returns 422 because GitHub can only attach existing repository labels. A repo-wide search finds no provisioning for either `ci-review-failed` or `ui-security-review-failed`, so the job fails without leaving the signal intended to replace the disabled `[aw]` issue; ensure both labels are created before these jobs can use them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for private security delivery before clearing the label**

When the agent emits `report_security_finding`, the Slack delivery runs in the separate generated `report_security_finding` job, but this label job depends only on `agent` and `safe_outputs`. If the webhook is absent, Slack rejects the payload, or the delivery job otherwise fails, this job can concurrently see a successful agent, successful public safe outputs, and non-empty `output_types`, then clear `ui-security-review-failed` even though the only copy of a security finding was not delivered privately. Include the private-report job's result in the dependency and failure decision.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard failure-label updates with current-head authority**

When a new commit is pushed while an earlier CI Review is running, the old and new reviews remain concurrent because the workflow's concurrency key includes the SHA, yet both mutate the same PR-wide label here. An older successful run can therefore remove the label set by a newer failed run, or an older failure can add a stale label after the newer head was reviewed successfully. Recheck that `needs.eligibility.outputs.head_sha` is still the PR head before changing the label, or otherwise serialize label ownership by head.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Paginate failed workflow runs before building the digest**

In a week with more than 100 failed workflow runs across the repository, this request returns only the first page and filtering happens afterward, so older scheduled agentic failures can be omitted entirely or undercounted. Since the digest is now the only replacement for the disabled failure issues on scheduled sweeps, follow the API pagination links and aggregate all pages within the bounded date window before filtering.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Trim the failure label job and the security-findings fragment to the essentials

Stop missing-tool, missing-data and incomplete reports from filing issues

The bare `false` form was dropped by gh-aw in workflows with custom safe-output
jobs, so the explicit `create-issue: false` form is used everywhere.
Only let the current head's CI Review run change the failure label

Not changing: adding a label that doesn't exist yet through the issue labels API creates it. The repo's `agentic-workflows` label was made that way, with the default colour `ededed` and no description.
Not changing: if the Slack job fails, the whole run fails and shows as a red check on the PR, and the weekly spend report counts it. The label only tracks whether a review was posted.

Fixed in a0cce0ca7: the job now does nothing unless `head_sha` is still the PR's head. UI Security Review doesn't need this because it uses one concurrency group per PR with cancel-in-progress, and a cancelled run skips the label job.
This code is gone: the digest section was dropped, and failures now appear as a column in the existing spend report.
Not changing: the column matches the report's existing all-runs-failed alert, which also counts only `failure`. A job that hits `timeout-minutes` ends the run as `failure`.
Fixed in a0cce0ca7: the job checks that `head_sha` is still the PR's head before it touches the label.

GitHub records timeout-minute exhaustion as the distinct `timed_out` conclusion, and this script preserves that value in `conclusions`. Matching the existing alert therefore reproduces the same omission; timed-out runs still display as zero failed. The proposed change remains applicable.

**Medium: Private findings exposed through artifacts and logs**

Any signed-in reader can retrieve findings submitted through this supposedly private tool: the importing workflows upload `safeoutputs.jsonl`, `agent_output.json`, and `agent-stdio.log` in the `agent` artifact—for example, `.github/workflows/pydantic-ai-bug-hunter.lock.yml:1109–1126`. The shim emits the full tool arguments into that log, and the pinned output collector additionally prints payload previews into job logs, so Slack access is not needed to read the report. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/managing-workflow-runs/downloading-workflow-artifacts))

Run security-bearing workflows in a private context, or ensure report payloads and their tool-call/reproduction traces are redacted or encrypted before any public logs, summaries, or artifact uploads.
